messages:
shayla: Heads up — #console shows a weird spike in fncall soft-rejects for routeId=customer-x. 60% soft rejects in the last hour vs ~5% baseline. Anyone digging?

kyle: Oof. Is that the new strict-validate canary? Which model/variant?

micah: I pulled a few traces. Telemetry tag is "validation.invalid_shape" and the payload we received is basically an array where our fnhook expects an object. quick sample: 
```json
["open_file", {"path":"/etc/passwd"}]
```
So adapter returns an array (old SDK client) and validator flags it as soft.

console-bot: alert: fncall.soft_reject_rate > 0.5 for routeId=customer-x (EU-WEST) — triggered at 2026-03-21T14:12:25Z :warning:

priya: Are we sure the dashboard isn’t under-sampling the raw event stream? The panel uses 1:100 sampling for debug payloads, but counts for billing are based on full ingest. Could be a telemetry sampling mismatch.

shayla: Good point. On the UI I see the sampled counts (small) but the rate chart uses the full rate. The mismatch makes it look like noisy rejects are overwhelming. We should show both — sampled messages and aggregate count.

micah: Also found the router was routing these to the degen variant (fallback-model) which has permissive parsing, so end-user isn't failing. But that still creates a soft_reject telemetry row and increments the "reject" counter. We need to decide: do soft_rejects count toward quota? Current code increments quota on original request path before fallback.

todd: We debated this in last sprint — semantics said: soft_reject = no billing penalty, hard_reject = billed. But implementation diverged. I can see code in route-handlers: 
```js
if (validation === 'soft') { metrics.increment('fncall.rejections'); }
```
That increments regardless.

kyle: That seems wrong. We should increment a separate metric (fncall.soft_rejects) and not affect billing. Customer-impact if they hit quota.

priya: For the console change: add a split in the panel: soft_rejects vs hard_rejects, and add a link that fetches a few sampled raw payloads (admin-only). UX microcopy: "Soft rejects: auto-fallbacked — not billed unless configured".

shayla: Quick mitigation? roll back the metric change or patch to exclude soft from billing count. Which is lower-risk?

micah: Patch is tiny: change metrics.increment('fncall.rejections') -> metrics.increment('fncall.hard_rejections') only for hard cases. I can ship a patch to the canary within 30 min.

console-bot: deploy started: eng-platform/canary-v2 -> eu-west at 2026-03-21T14:23:10Z (micah) :rocket:

todd: We also need a short-term dashboard annotation explaining sampling differences (priya, can you add?) so SRE/CS doesn't misinterpret.

priya: Yep, I'll add note + show raw counts toggle. Also will add a tooltip that explains billing semantics.

kyle: After patch, run a backfill sanity check on the last 24h to recompute billed counts vs displayed. Might need a correction job.

shayla: Action items: 1) micah deploy metric change to canary (in progress) 2) priya update panel + tooltip 3) kyle schedule backfill check 4) todd confirm quota logic tests. If canary looks good, promote to prod.

micah: Canary up. Early signal looks like soft_rejects metric emitted separate series, and quota counts unaffected on test traffic. Will monitor for 1h.

shayla: Thanks. If anyone sees a customer escalation open a P0 channel and ping me.

todd: filing a quick follow-up doc in eng-platform runbook regarding fncall billing semantics so this doesn't bit us again.

priya: Added dashboard note and raw toggle. leaving a comment on the panel with the link to this thread. :white_check_mark:

console-bot: deploy success: eng-platform/canary-v2 -> eu-west at 2026-03-21T14:27:20Z (micah) :tada:

shayla: Great work team — keep an eye on customer-x and overall EU-WEST. Closing thread if no regressions in 1h.
